summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student language model on its own responses, guided by a fixed teacher. Generating these responses is expensive, so systems use quantized inference and asynchronous rollouts to reduce the cost.
takeaways: Both, however, introduce training-inference mismatch between the rollout engine and the model being trained.
Such mismatch can destabilize reinforcement learning (RL), but its effects on OPD remain unclear.
Model-specific FP8 recipes preserve training quality while providing capacity for at least 1.93times as many KV-cache tokens as BF16.
